title: Inkling 2 Mini API Pricing in 2026 and Extra Costs
summary: Inkling 2 Mini API pricing covers plans with different per-token rates and limits. The confirmed data shows costs to estimate your monthly bill.
body_markdown:
## Cap Inkling 2 Mini spend with Activepieces


Left alone, the overrun turns up on the invoice, after you've spent it.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/inkling-2-mini-vs-inkling-2-small-pricing-comparison) can watch your Inkling 2 Mini spend at 1 credit per flow run, so a ten-step check costs what a two-step one does; the meter is the run, not the steps inside it.


It's an automation tool that connects apps through step-by-step workflows, and it can't lower the price, so set the vendor's own limits first.


Start where the money is counted. Do these in order, and check each screen against the pricing page on the date you do it, since plan rules change.


1. Open the vendor's usage dashboard and read what your team consumed last month, broken out by day if it allows.
2. Set a billing alert, so an email reaches you before the month closes.
3. Set a hard limit, so the account stops serving requests at a ceiling you chose. Know what stops: a hard limit protects your budget, and it also means a customer-facing feature goes dark when it trips.


An alert tells you the bill is climbing. **A hard limit is the only part that actually stops it, so don't skip it because the alert feels like enough.**


### Log usage per workflow


Here Activepieces earns its place. Its HTTP step, a block that sends a request to any web address, can call the Inkling 2 Mini API from inside a workflow.


Each API response reports how many tokens, the small chunks of text the model bills by, that call used.


Add an HTTP step to the workflow that calls the API, and log the tokens used on each call to a spreadsheet, with a column for the workflow name.


Now you can see the usual culprit, one chatty workflow hiding in a dozen, because the sheet shows which workflow is spending, which the vendor's dashboard may not split out for you.


### Inkling 2 Mini spend alerts before quota limits


Add a threshold alert: a step that totals the sheet and messages you when spend crosses a line you set below the hard limit. Review the sheet weekly, five minutes, same day each week.


Set that line well under the hard limit, so the warning arrives while you can still change something. The weekly review catches slow drift that no single alert will.


This setup monitors the bill. It doesn't change the price, the plan tier or the usage limits. Those come from the pricing page, so check it again on the day you decide.


The logging and alert steps cost nothing extra to run, because Activepieces meters the run, not the steps inside it: 1 credit per flow run, so the free plan's 1,000 credits a month cover the flow whether it has three steps or thirty.


Zapier bills per task and Make per module, so on their pricing pages every added logging or alert step becomes a line on the bill.
